title: ARR Waterfall Scenario Analysis
summary: Build multi-scenario stress tests from an ARR Waterfall model (or generate seed data from scratch). Creates 3 market-specific headwind scenario tabs, quarterly ARR comparison charts, impact/valuation tables with conditional highlighting, acceleration assumptions driver table, and detailed assumption breakdowns. Includes guardrails for growth rates and formula validation. Pacer AI Foundation branding or bring your own colors.
prompt:
IMPORTANT: This skill is designed to work with Pacer AI ARR Waterfall Modeling by Market. For optimal use forecasting by Market, please contact Will@getpacerai.com or build a Roll-Forward financial model at the customer-product level to show: Beginning of Period, Churn, Product Churn, Downsell, Upsell, Cross-sell, New Logo, End of Period, and Net New.

SEED DATA: If the user does not provide a workbook, ask: What ARR size business do you want to model? (e.g., $10M, $50M, $200M). Generate a complete Modeling tab with 3 markets, 12 months, 20-30% baseline growth. Insert disclaimer: This generative AI data and calculations have not been reviewed by the team at Pacer AI.

TERMINOLOGY: Use ARR (not MRR) in all display text, row labels, chart titles, and headers.

BRANDING: Before formatting charts, ask the user: Do you want to use Pacer AI branding (dark theme with teal/blue/green palette) or do you have your own brand colors?

GUARDRAILS: Baseline ARR growth must not exceed 40% (ideal 20-30%). Ending ARR = Beg ARR + Churn + Product Churn + Downsell + Upsell + Cross-sell + New Logo ARR. Net New ARR = Ending ARR - Beginning ARR. Bold Beg/End ARR rows. Show % of Beg ARR in adjacent column. Valuation highlighting: 3.5x if growth <12%, 4.0x if 12-18%, 4.5x if >18%.

Build a Scenario Analysis from my ARR Waterfall model.

Source: The "Modeling" tab contains a monthly ARR roll-forward model with 3 markets (Market A, Market B, Market C). Each market has the same structure:

Market A: Rows 16–23 (Beg ARR row 16, assumptions rows 17–22: Churn%, Product Churn%, Downsell%, Upsell%, Cross-sell%, New%, Ending ARR row 23)
Market B: Rows 47–54 (same structure, Beg ARR row 47, Ending ARR row 54)
Market C: Rows 78–85 (same structure, Beg ARR row 78, Ending ARR row 85)
Total Ending ARR: Row 115 (=sum of 3 market Ending ARR rows)
2025 quarters end at columns: N (Q1), O (Q2), R (Q3), U (Q4)
2026 months start at column AK (Jan) through AV (Dec). Quarter-end columns: AM (Q1), AP (Q2), AS (Q3), AV (Q4)
Baseline assumption rows for each market reference column J for the historical rate (e.g., J20 = Upsell%, J21 = Cross-sell%, J22 = New%)

What to build:

Step 1 — Create 3 Scenario Tabs (duplicate "Modeling" tab 3 times):

Scenario 1: Market A headwinds
Scenario 2: Market B headwinds
Scenario 3: Market C headwinds

Each scenario tab gets driver rows in W1:

Row 1: Scenario title (e.g., "Scenario 1: Market A New Logo -0.1%/mo from Apr")
Row 2: New Logo % override — Jan-Mar (X2) = baseline from J (e.g., =J22 for S1, =J53 for S2, =J84 for S3), then Apr onward declines -0.1%/mo (=X2-0.001, =X2-0.002, ..., =X2-0.009)
Row 3: Upsell % override — Jan-Mar = 0, Apr onward = -0.001, -0.002, ..., -0.009
Row 4: Cross-sell % override — Jan-Mar = 0, Apr onward = -0.001, -0.002, ..., -0.009

Wire the TARGET market's assumption rows to driver rows:

S1: Market A rows 20-22 for 2026 (columns X): Row 22 (New%) =XX2 (direct), Row 20 (Upsell%) =MAX(0,$J$20+XX$3), Row 21 (Cross-sell%) =MAX(0,$J$21+XX$4)
S2: Market B rows 51-53: Same pattern referencing $J$51, $J$52, $J$53
S3: Market C rows 82-84: Same pattern referencing $J$82, $J$83, $J$84
Non-target markets keep their original formulas unchanged
Q1 2026 (Jan-Mar) MUST be identical across all tabs — driver rows are 0%/baseline for first 3 months, divergence starts April

Step 2 — Create "Scenario Charts" tab with this layout:

Rows 1-5: Quarterly ARR chart data

Row 1: Quarter labels — C1 = "Q1 '25", "Q2 '25", "Q3 '25", "Q4 '25", "Q1 '26", "Q2 '26", "Q3 '26", "Q4 '26"
Row 2 (Base Case): =Modeling!{col}115*12 for each quarter-end column (N, O, R, U for 2025; AM, AP, AS, AV for 2026)
Row 3 (Scenario 1): 2025 same as Base, 2026 = ='Scenario 1'!{col}115*12
Row 4 (Scenario 2): Same pattern from Scenario 2 tab
Row 5 (Scenario 3): Same pattern from Scenario 3 tab
Labels in B2: "Base Case ARR", "Scenario 1", "Scenario 2", "Scenario 3"
Colors (default Pacer AI Foundation — ask user if they prefer their own): Base=#27899A (Teal), S1=#4A90D9 (Steel Blue), S2=#2DB87A (Growth Green), S3=#70C49C (Teal Light). Background=#080E1C, borders=#1E2D4A, text=#CDD5E0

Create a line chart from B1:J5:
Y-axis format: $#,##0.0,,M (millions)
Match series colors to the 4-color scheme above

Rows 29-42: Impact Table

Row 30: Header "Impact" (bold, underlined)
Layout per scenario (rows 32, 34, 36, 38 with blank separator rows):
Column B: Scenario name + description (e.g., "Baseline: Continue trendline", "Scenario 1: Headwinds of 0.1% in Market A starting in Q2")
Column F: "ARR Growth" header (row 30) — formula: =(J{row}-$F$2)/$F$2 (YoY: Dec '26 ARR vs Q4 '25 ARR). Format: 0.0%
Column H: "ARR" header (row 30) — formula: =J{row} (Dec '26 ARR). Format: $#,##0
Columns J-L: "Valuation: Dec '26 ARR/EV" header (row 30)
Row 31: Multiples — 3.5, 4, 4.5 (format: 0.0"x", bold)
Valuation rows: =ROUND($H{row}*{col}$31,-4). Format: $#,##0

Rows 48+: Detailed Assumptions by Scenario (4 blocks: Baseline, S1, S2, S3):

Each block has:
Title row (e.g., "Baseline:", "Scenario 1")
Column headers: Q1 '26 through Q4 '26 (plus Q4 '25 for context)
Rows: Beg ARR, Churn, Product Churn, Downsell, Upsell, Cross-sell, New, Ending ARR, Net New ARR, GRR, NRR
All values reference their respective tab's quarter-end columns

Formatting: Aptos Narrow 11pt throughout. Font colors match scenario colors for chart data rows. Number formats: $#,##0 for ARR, 0.0% for growth rates and retention metrics, 0.0"x" for multiples.
variables: Modeling tab with ARR roll-forward model (or request seed data)
Market row ranges (default: A=16-23, B=47-54, C=78-85)
Brand colors (optional — defaults to Pacer AI Foundation theme)
